  - classifyListing(pending, listing) -&gt; Present|AbsentCandidate|NoAction; only complete declared coverage can yield AbsentCandidate, never a terminal outcome.
- effectBoundary: Scheduler and broker-spi perform listing/getOrder effects under leases; pure classification decides candidate and outcome. Query projections never issue ad hoc polling.
- durability: Persist job dedup key, notBefore, attempt, lease epoch, listing snapshot identity, and observation outcome. Repeated listing passes do not create duplicate confirm jobs for the same order.
- errors:

  - PresentOrder is StillWorking, not Filled.
  - ListingCoverageUnknown/ListingPartial retains pending orders and schedules follow-up; it never emits Cancelled from an empty array.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve one-listing efficiency and no repeated getOrder for known-working orders.
  - Make absence conservative rather than silently terminal.
- replacementSteps:

- verificationCases:

  - A Partial/Unavailable listing or lagging null confirmation remains Unknown/StillWorking and never triggers redispatch.
  - A listing that omits a declared namespace is Partial and cannot select absence candidates; a complete scoped listing still requires per-order confirmation before terminal state.

- targetModel: ClosePosition is CloseTarget{quantity: Quantity|All, InstrumentId, AccountScope, riskClass: ReduceOnly} with ExposureSnapshot and ExposureEquals precondition. PreparedCloseStep carries the snapshot, conflict key Exposure, compensation assessment, and the adapter evidence that native close cannot cross through flat. ExposureVersionEvidence is MonotonicNativeVersion|FactHashOnly; the prepared close persists the evidence kind, canonical fact hash, and source observation identity, with strong-version policy refusing a hash-only adapter.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeClose(qty) -&gt; Quantity or All; reject nonfinite/nonpositive.
  - prepareClose(observedExposure,target,capability) -&gt; PreparedClose or Precondition/CapabilityFailure; compare exposure again at admission using a supplied observation.
  - evolveCloseObservation(previous,remoteOutcome) -&gt; terminal/residual/reconciling state; an effectful close call is not a pure transition.
  - compareExposure(expected, observed, evidencePolicy) -&gt; Satisfied|PreconditionFailed|ExposureVersionUnproven; FactHashOnly never masquerades as a monotonic broker version.
- effectBoundary: Broker-spi observe reads exposure; compiler and pure precondition evaluation do not. Close interpreter mutation occurs only after DispatchStarted. Application query returns typed exposure views.
- durability: Exposure snapshot/version, lock, dispatch attempt, and observation are durable. If close result is Unknown, retain lock in Reconciling and never issue an unobserved reverse action.
- errors:
  - InvalidQuantity{raw}; caller fixes request.
  - PreconditionFailed{expectedExposure,observedExposure}; re-prepare.
  - NativeReduceOnlyUnavailable; refuse dispatch rather than rely on a close verb.
  - OutcomeUnknown{dispatchId}; reconciliation required.
  - ExposureVersionUnproven and StaleExposureObservation require re-observation/reprepare and create no DispatchStarted.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve positive partial/full-close semantics and the no-oversize safety check.
  - Require explicit ReduceOnly/native safety evidence; never assume an adapter will enforce it from the action name.
  - Replace “no broker call” as the only proof with a durable precondition failure and no dispatch job.
- replacementSteps:
  - Make quantity decoder and exposure comparison pure; persist snapshot and conflict key.
  - Test race where broker quantity decreases after prepare.
  - Retain Decimal precision in Quantity codec.
- verificationCases:
  - Quantity 11 against exposure 10 returns PreconditionFailed and no DispatchStarted.
  - After prepare at exposure 10, an admission observation of 4 rejects quantity 5 before DispatchStarted; an adapter without reduce-only evidence is also refused.
  - All closes current exposure but a later observation shows residual due to partial fill; the residual remains durable.
  - Crash after DispatchStarted leaves Reconciling, not a second close.
  - A broker with no monotonic version can use the canonical fact-hash path only when policy permits weak evidence; a strong-version policy rejects it before dispatch.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Source evidence services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.spec.ts:247-298: close tests pass Decimal quantity, perform live position lookup, reject oversized/stale partial close before broker call, and pass undefined for full close. is covered: the source validates live exposure and full-close undefined quantity; the target models Quantity|All with ExposureEquals and refuses dispatch without native reduce-only evidence. Design falsifier: Quantity 11 against exposure 10 returns PreconditionFailed and no DispatchStarted. Remaining open point is an external adapter/config/accounting fact; the target keeps it unavailable or blocks the action until evidence exists. Closure makes the exposure-version fallback explicit: monotonic native versions are optional evidence, canonical fact hashes are weaker, and strong-CAS policy refuses unproven adapters.

- problem: A currency equality check treats same labels as enough evidence and has no FX rate provenance or valuation timestamp; mutating AccountInfo mixes adapter data and derived accounting.
- targetModel: Use Money{amount:DecimalString,currency:CurrencyCode} and the closed Valuation ADT: BrokerReported{money,observedAt}; Derived{money,inputs,fxEvidence,asOf}; or DerivedUnavailable{brokerReported,reason}. Valuation records FxPolicy{providerId/pair,maxAge,rounding,version} and FxRateObservation provenance; no provider, quote currency, or freshness value is inferred from a label.

  - projectAccount(events) -&gt; AccountView with the valuation variant and checkpoint; no query-side mutation.
  - aggregatePnL(accountMoney, positionMoney, fxResult, policy) -&gt; Derived|BrokerReported|DerivedUnavailable; Stale/Unavailable/UnknownFx cannot enter Derived.
- effectBoundary: Broker account/position and FX reads are Effects; currency arithmetic and valuation selection are pure. A refresh/observation command may write through JournalWriter, but the account query itself only reads projections and cannot append reconcile events.
- durability: Persist account/position/FX observations and derived valuation evidence in the observation/projection writer path with as-of and source sequence; do not overwrite broker data without recording the derivation. Missing FX retains BrokerReported plus DerivedUnavailable.

  - ValuationStale; caller chooses freshness policy.
  - MoneyCurrencyMismatch is a programmer/data boundary failure.

- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve exact same-currency sum behavior when all evidence is same base currency.
  - Preserve broker value for mixed books until FX evidence exists, but make the reason visible.
- replacementSteps:

- currentBehavior: Guard pipeline wraps direct dispatch; blocked operation returns rejected and placeOrder is not called, while allowed operation reaches the broker.
- problem: Guard execution is an in-process mutable pipeline after Git commit; it does not prove pure prepare-time policy, capability evidence, or durable no-job behavior.
- targetModel: Model GuardDecision{Allowed|Denied(issue)} as a pure policy step over typed action, Actor, AccountScope, and facts. A separate ReservationRequest/ReservationResult boundary reserves cooldown/risk capacity durably only after guard approval; Prepare aggregates risk/capability/precondition decisions before creating any dispatch job. GuardPolicy is the C08 versioned ADT with CooldownPolicy, GrossNotional exposure, and InstrumentWhitelistPolicy; unknown facts produce PolicyFactUnavailable rather than a pass.
- pureTransitions:
  - evaluateGuards(action, policy, facts) -&gt; Allowed or ValidationFailed/CapabilityUnavailable.
  - decidePrepare(guardResult) -&gt; TransactionPrepared or PrepareRejected; no scheduler effect for Denied.
  - evaluateGuards(action, policy, facts) -&gt; Allowed|Denied|PolicyFactUnavailable; reservation submission is separate and occurs only for an approved execution intent.
- effectBoundary: Policy evaluation is pure; facts (symbol catalog, equity, cooldown, exposure) come from explicit application queries. Reservation submission/release is a durable writer Effect keyed by transaction/revision, and broker dispatch receives only an admitted prepared step.
- durability: Persist guard policy/version and decision evidence in PreparedPlan/receipt; if a reservation is needed, reserve and its release/expiry are durable idempotent events. Rejected plans have no DispatchPlanned, EffectJob, or lock; unknown guard facts block rather than consume a reservation.
- errors:
  - GuardDenied{guardType, issue}; caller corrects action.
  - PolicyFactUnavailable; prepare is blocked rather than allowed by unknown.
  - CooldownActive, MaxExposureExceeded, InstrumentResolutionRequired, and PolicyFactUnavailable are exhaustive; missing symbol never means allow.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve whitelist rejection and allowed AAPL dispatch.
  - Change guard call-count/spy proof to durable admission proof and prevent unknown symbol/equity from silently passing.
- replacementSteps:
  - Split guard pure functions from effectful fact collection.
  - Add tests for denial after stale facts and for policy version in plan digest.
- verificationCases:
  - TSLA produces PrepareRejected and zero reservations/effect jobs; AAPL produces one admitted PlaceOrder with a durable reservation only when policy requires it.
  - If whitelist catalog is unavailable, result is typed PolicyFactUnavailable and neither broker nor reservation writer is invoked.
  - A later guard rejection does not consume cooldown; unknown mark/FX/equity blocks prepare; TSLA/ambiguous modify identity is denied before reservation or broker dispatch.

## Cross-group contracts

- K01: Each CoreAccount capability is a declaration that supplies its own exact input/output/error schemas, semantic unit, handler and resource needs; data readers and controlled effects compose separately, and adding a provider leaf must not edit a kernel switch.
- K02: The UTA-facing fixed CapabilityDescriptor envelope is shared, but provider trees remain open-ended. CoreAccount must not introduce a global ActionContractMap or require every provider to implement empty broker handlers; the source IBroker/global switch is retained only as currentBehavior evidence.
- K03: Zod/JSON-schema declarations are the source for validation, static types, metadata and CLI projections. Native order, instrument and error fields survive as exact provider extensions; SDK Contract/Order values are adapter-bound and never journaled.
- K04: Order, Candle, Instrument and related units are composable contracts, not a closed order-combination catalogue. Quantity/notional, protection, TIF and relation choices are provider-declared HOF/schema combinations; AccountScope is required for account/order effects only, while public data carries explicit Public or schema-declared context.
- K05: Account/position/order/catalog reads are pull data or resource-scoped push streams with explicit freshness, cursor, coverage, backpressure and recovery evidence. They do not use prepare/approve/compensate, effect locks or per-frame WAL.
- K06: Generated CLI/help/describe views must come from the same declared capability tree. Pull returns finite schema data and push returns lifecycle-aware frames; CLI cancellation releases its read resource without cancelling an already accepted trading effect.
- K07: Broker adapters may retain native SDK/protocol/process boundaries. Only the selected declared leaf handler crosses that boundary; load/input/output/delivery errors and post-dispatch Unknown remain distinct, and method presence never proves idempotency or atomicity.
- K08: Durable intent, approval, dispatch, WAL/CAS/idempotency, reconciliation and compensation apply only to controlled trading effects. Data-cache or observation failure cannot trigger transaction compensation; native guarantees remain evidence-qualified.
- K09: A trigger/event source is not authority. If CoreAccount later participates in a trigger binding, activation must carry frozen intent/revision, scope and policy evidence and pass the normal execution authorization path.
- K10: ReturnToAgent is a durable unsent-order review branch with stable ReviewRequest/outbox identity and explicit retain/rearm/revise/discard/request-submission commands; it creates no broker dispatch and does not claim AI delivery.
- K11: Existing source facts, durability boundaries, unknown/precision/absence obligations and open native questions remain evidence. Reframing removes obsolete universal-SDK conclusions without declaring sibling ownership or empirical gaps solved.
- K12: CoreAccount verificationCases are future falsifiers only: prove declaration-derived type/validator/metadata changes, public-vs-account scope, data pull/push separation, native schema validation, unknown barriers and ReturnToAgent zero-dispatch behavior; no runtime proof was run here.

## Additional findings

- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:37: side-effect import contract-ext augments the native Contract shape; the cutover must move this augmentation to the broker adapter/protocol boundary so domain codecs do not depend on SDK prototype mutation.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:993-1004: the account-PnL comment states wallet-sourced broker PnL is a placeholder zero and that deriving from positions costs one extra broker round trip; the target account query must retain this explicit consistency goal while recording currency/FX provenance and query cost.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1033-1039: wallet reconciliation is documented as an in-place mutation of broker positions because cost basis lives in the order log; target design must separate immutable observation, journaled accounting evolution, and response projection.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1108-1114: the reconcile helper exists only because GitCommit requires stateAfter and intentionally avoids recursive broker reads; replacing Git requires an event payload that carries real observed facts rather than reintroducing recursive query writes.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1157-1163: expansion has hub-to-leaf semantics and passes hub keys verbatim because directories are not tradeable; catalog ADTs must preserve this distinction and must not route hub keys through native trade-contract resolution.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1187-1192: refreshCatalog is intended as an optional broker-side cache refresh and should resolve for server-side-search brokers; target API must make that Unsupported/NoRefresh capability explicit rather than silently claiming freshness.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1205-1209: the aliceId-only expansion path is shared by in-process, AI-tool, and HTTP-route callers; protocol decoder and adapter compiler must be the single replacement path so these callers cannot diverge.
- Cross-group accounting invariant: ReconcileBalance is a valuation/accounting estimate with explicit valuationOnly provenance, never a synthetic FillObservation or remote execution claim; query paths read projections while observation/reconciliation workers own journal writes.
- Cross-group lifecycle invariant: RuntimeHealth describes process startup/recovery/shutdown, BrokerHealthView describes scoped connection evidence, and neither health variant alone grants action capability or resolves Unknown transaction outcomes.
- Scope boundary finding: account/order observations and controlled effects carry AccountScope; public Candle/News/Instrument-like leaves use Public or their declared context and never synthesize accountId/subAccountId.
- Composition finding: the fixed descriptor envelope is the only UTA-facing common surface. Provider-specific trees, schemas, errors, native fields and handlers remain adapter-owned; the historical UTA IBroker switch is not a target contract.
